issues.body:
The row asserts `grep -Ec 'actionlint_bin=\$\(_ensure_actionlint\)$'` over `$gate_body`, where `gate_body=$(declare -f registry_selftest_gate)`, and expects 0.

`declare -f` re-prints the parsed function: an AND-OR list is emitted on a SINGLE line and backslash-newline continuations do not survive. The pre-change source was

    [[ -n "$actionlint_bin" ]] || actionlint_bin=$(_ensure_actionlint) \
      || die "actionlint unavailable and pinned provisioning failed: $name (...)"

which `declare -f` renders as one line ending in the `die "..."` string. The `$` anchor therefore never matched the old form either, so the count is 0 both before and after this diff. The assertion cannot flip red for the condition it names.

This is not hypothetical formatting trivia — the diff itself is evidence: the two POSITIVE rows immediately above deliberately switch to `gate_source_body=$(_shell_function_body "$SCRIPT_DIR/worker-live.sh" registry_selftest_gate)` precisely because their expected strings end in a trailing `\`, which `declare -f` would have eaten. The same reasoning invalidates the `$`-anchored negative.

The row is not redundant with the positive one: the positive assertion pins that the NEW target-tree call site exists, but does not forbid an ADDITIONAL bare `_ensure_actionlint` provisioning site elsewhere in the gate — which is exactly the mutant this row is supposed to catch, and cannot.

By contrast the sibling negative row ('no longer preflights the ORCHESTRATOR requirement table') uses an unanchored substring `"$SELFTEST_ENV_REQUIREMENTS" "$SCRIPT_DIR"`, which does survive the collapse and is genuinely non-vacuous. Only the actionlint one is broken.
issues.fix_hint: Either (a) drop the `$` anchor and match the unanchored substring on `$gate_body`, e.g. `grep -Fc 'actionlint_bin=$(_ensure_actionlint)'` expecting 0 — note this must be an exact-string (-F) match so the new `_ACTIONLINT_PIN_FILE=... _ensure_actionlint` form does not also count; or (b) run the negative against `$gate_source_body` (the source-parsed body), where the line really does end at the continuation, keeping the `$` anchor meaningful. Then PROVE it is non-vacuous the way the dispatch pin does: add a fixture function body carrying the orchestrator-pin form and assert the check reports `caught` on it, so a future refactor of `_shell_function_body`/`declare -f` output cannot silently re-vacuum the row.
issues.title: Vacuous self-test: the '#1576 wiring: no longer provisions from the ORCHESTRATOR actionlint pin' row passes on the OLD code too

issues.body:
The new call site is

    || actionlint_bin=$(_ACTIONLINT_PIN_FILE="$tree_scripts/actionlint.pin" _ensure_actionlint) \

where `$tree_scripts` is `$PWD/scripts`, i.e. the candidate checkout the model just wrote and that no human has reviewed yet.

Two load-bearing comments in the same file now state the opposite and were not touched:

* :2168-2170 — "Still checked-in, still never env-supplied: the path below is derived from SCRIPT_DIR, not from the environment, so nothing PR- or env-controlled can swap in a different artifact."
* :2308-2309 — "the sole production call site passes no arguments, so nothing PR- or env-controlled can swap the pins."

After this diff the production call site DOES env-supply the pin path, and the pin it resolves IS PR-controlled. A reviewer or future agent auditing the actionlint provisioning path will read a guarantee that no longer holds — on the trust surface, in the lane that runs before any review.

The substantive change is defensible: pr-gate.yml also reads the PR checkout's `scripts/actionlint.pin`, so the two lanes agree, and `_actionlint_pin` still constrains the version to `[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)*` (no traversal, no host control — the URL host/path are fixed) and both digests are still verified. But the residual exposure is real and undocumented: a candidate tree can now choose WHICH genuine actionlint release the orchestrator downloads and executes, including a downgrade to a release with weaker checks, with self-consistent digests that the checksum verification cannot detect (the attacker supplies both the artifact selector and the expected hash). That trade needs to be written down where the old guarantee was, not left silently inverted.
issues.fix_hint: Update both comment blocks to state the post-#1576 threat model explicitly: the pin path is now supplied by the caller and resolves inside the TARGET TREE; digest pinning still prevents an unverified artifact but no longer prevents a candidate from selecting the artifact, and the compensating control is that `scripts/actionlint.pin` is a reviewed diff (same as pr-gate.yml's lane) plus the version-shape constraint that keeps the URL host/path fixed. Consider also asserting in the gate that the resolved pin path is under `$PWD/scripts` (reject an absolute/`..` escape) so the seam cannot later be widened past the target tree, and add a self-test row pinning that the only production env-supply of `_ACTIONLINT_PIN_FILE` is the `$tree_scripts` one.
issues.title: _ACTIONLINT_PIN_FILE is now env-supplied from a PR-controlled path, contradicting the unchanged trust comments at :2168-2170 and :2308-2309

issues.body:
The diff rewires three policy inputs to the target tree and adds wiring assertions for only two of them:

* dependency preflight table + suite -> asserted (`"$tree_env_requirements" "$tree_scripts" "$tree_suite"); then`)
* actionlint pin -> asserted (positively; the negative is broken, see the blocker)
* `SELFTEST_ENV_REQUIREMENTS="$tree_env_requirements" _assert_worker_image_gate_deps "$name"` -> NOT asserted

The only existing coverage of that call site is the pre-existing `grep -c '_assert_worker_image_gate_deps'` expecting 1, which stays green whether or not the env prefix is present. So dropping the prefix — reverting the worker-image gate-deps check to grading the ORCHESTRATOR's requirement table against the CANDIDATE's Dockerfile — produces a fully green suite. That is precisely the class of undetected revert the #1576 wiring rows exist to prevent, and it is the check that decides whether the model container will be able to run the suite at all.

Compounding this, the coupling is implicit: `_assert_worker_image_gate_deps` reads the global `SELFTEST_ENV_REQUIREMENTS` at :1839 rather than taking the table as a parameter, and its own docstring at :1827-1829 still describes it as deriving from "SELFTEST_ENV_REQUIREMENTS" with no mention that the caller may now shadow it. A bash temporary assignment on a function call is also not scope-stable across modes (under `set -o posix` the assignment PERSISTS after the call), which makes the idiom a poor carrier for a trust-plane policy input.
issues.fix_hint: Give `_assert_worker_image_gate_deps` an explicit table parameter — `local file=$1 table=${2:-$SELFTEST_ENV_REQUIREMENTS}` and read `<<< "$table"` — then call it as `_assert_worker_image_gate_deps "$name" "$tree_env_requirements"`, which is greppable and mode-independent. Add the matching wiring row alongside the other two #1576 rows, asserting the exact target-tree call form appears once and that no orchestrator-table form remains; and extend the existing `_assert_worker_image_gate_deps` self-tests with one row proving a CANDIDATE table (a row the orchestrator's table does not contain) is what drives the verdict.
issues.title: The third rewired policy input (worker-image dep check) has no wiring assertion — a silent revert to the orchestrator table goes undetected

issues.body:
The four new rows drive the reader with synthetic fixtures only (candidate/duplicate/unterminated/empty). Nothing asserts that the function successfully reads THIS file's own `SELFTEST_ENV_REQUIREMENTS` block — the one production input it will always be handed, and the one whose shape is most likely to drift.

That shape is load-bearing and fragile in ways the fixtures do not exercise: the real table spans two physical lines inside one single-quoted string, so it depends on `[^']*` crossing a newline; and `$` under `re.M` must land exactly after the closing quote, so a trailing comment or trailing whitespace on the terminating line would silently make the whole gate die 'target-tree SELFTEST_ENV_REQUIREMENTS is unreadable'. That is fail-closed, which is the right direction, but it converts a harmless whitespace edit into a hard gate refusal with no self-test warning anyone in advance.

Relatedly, the `len(matches) != 1` rule means the reader also refuses if a future edit ever adds a second column-0 assignment (for example a documented default in a comment-free block) — worth a row so the constraint is visible as a deliberate policy rather than discovered at gate time.
issues.fix_hint: Add one row asserting `_selftest_env_requirements_from_script "$SCRIPT_DIR/worker-live.sh"` equals the live `$SELFTEST_ENV_REQUIREMENTS` global — a direct round-trip that proves the multi-line real table parses and that parse and global cannot drift apart. Optionally add a fixture with a trailing comment after the closing quote asserting it REFUSES, so the strictness of the `'$` anchor is pinned as intended behaviour.
issues.title: _selftest_env_requirements_from_script is untested against the real worker-live.sh it must parse in production

verdict.summary: The core rewiring is right and closes a real hole: registry_selftest_gate previously derived its suite from the ORCHESTRATOR's manifest and ran every enrolled self-test out of SCRIPT_DIR, so the graded candidate's own scripts were largely never executed. Sourcing the candidate worker-live.sh to recover its policy table would have executed untrusted text before the sandbox, and the new _selftest_env_requirements_from_script correctly PARSES it instead, refusing missing/duplicated/unterminated/empty tables (four non-vacuous rows). The suite/root/table/pin inputs now all come from $PWD, matching pr-gate.yml's lane. Candidate-controlled probe/pattern strings stay quoted and reach only `command -v`, `python3 -c ... "$probe"` and `grep -Eq --`, so no shell-injection seam is opened, and _selftest_requirement_apt_package still fails closed on an unrecognised row. Three defects block approval. (1) The negative wiring row at the '#1576 wiring: the gate no longer provisions from the ORCHESTRATOR actionlint pin' check is VACUOUS: it greps `declare -f` output with an end-of-line anchor, but bash's pretty-printer collapses `A || B || C` onto one line and drops backslash continuations, so the old `actionlint_bin=$(_ensure_actionlint)` was never at end-of-line either. It reports 0 before and after the change. (2) The production call site now env-supplies _ACTIONLINT_PIN_FILE from a PR-controlled path, directly inverting the load-bearing comments at scripts/worker-live.sh:2168-2170 and :2308-2309, which still assert that nothing PR- or env-controlled can swap the pins. The invariant changed; the documentation of it did not. (3) The third rewired policy input, the target-tree table handed to _assert_worker_image_gate_deps, has no wiring assertion at all, unlike the other two.
